label: copy-phase steps re-reading an echoed token from a preferred set (j,k,h,r,d,y,n,b,i,a) or about to output j/b/h
explanation: Copy-phase feature: 99% of activation mass is in the copy phase (t > L), where about 25% of steps are active. It is almost silent in the original phase and at the <DEL> step, and never fires at t=0,1. Within the copy phase, whether it fires depends on token identity. The input token (the echoed original token) matters most: j (45% firing rate), then k, h, r, d, y, n, b. The token being output also matters: j, b, h, 0, u. Firing is more likely early in recall (recall_idx 1-2: about 35%) and drops for later positions. The largest activations (up to 0.60) come when j is echoed right after <DEL>, as in sequences starting j b / j j / c j, with the next token also strongly active. Because the token preference is graded and not a clean set, any token-set predicate leaves a lot of false positives and misses (dev F1 about 0.65, mass recall about 0.86). It does not depend on digit count, repeated tokens, or L.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=15: j, r, k, h; t=13: j, h, k, r; t=14: j, h, k, r) and the token being output (most: j, b, h, 0, u, f; least: c, t, o, x); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, phase=2, t=4.
